summary: Team LEXIA developed LEXIA ASTRO-SHIELD, a 100% offline medical and mental health co-pilot integrating flexible, dry-contact nanoconductor biosensors inside the spacesuit helmet liner and inner garment. During Mars missions, a 14m 22s One-Way Light Time creates nearly 29 minutes of communication silence with zero live flight-surgeon, tele-psychiatry, or cloud AI access, while crews face severe isolation, cortisol drift, and over 60% Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-Ocular Syndrome (SANS) risk. Addressing the astronaut health monitoring challenge, our platform calibrates five physiological suit zones using NASA OSDR, NASA HRP, CSA, ESA, and JAXA science into a deterministic 0 to 100 Biophysical Integration Variable (VIB) readiness score with zero AI hallucinations. It guides autonomous 0.1 Hz Cognitive Harmonization System (SAC) neuro-stabilization, digital Amsler eye checks, and Carlota Factor local AES-256 privacy before sending compact Earth alerts. This innovation prevents cognitive failure and vision loss in deep space while bringing zero-internet medical triage to rural and disaster communities on Earth.
details:
What It Does and How It Works LEXIA ASTRO-SHIELD is a 100% offline medical and mental health co-pilot designed for deep-space missions. Flexible, dry-contact nanoconductor sensors woven inside the spacesuit helmet liner and inner garment capture real-time neural coherence, dermal sweat cortisol, cardiac Heart Rate Variability (HRV), radiation dosimetry, and muscular telemetry offline. A deterministic edge engine fuses five physiological suit zones—Helmet Brain and SANS (25%), Thorax Heart and HRV (25%), Arm Radiation Badge (20%), Dermal Cortisol Patch (15%), and Limb Muscle Sensors (15%)—into an auditable 0 to 100 Biophysical Integration Variable (VIB) score. Scores of 75 to 100 confirm Nominal Operations; scores of 50 to 74 activate autonomous in-suit self-care via the Cognitive Harmonization System (SAC) using 0.1 Hz (4s/6s) respiratory-visual pacing, circadian light, or hydration prompts; and scores below 50 trigger an instant Red Critical Veto for storm shelter entry and priority Earth Flight Surgeon alerts.

Key Benefits The system operates with zero cloud dependency during 28m 44s round-trip Mars communication blackouts and eliminates generative AI medical hallucinations through deterministic triage rules. It catches Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-Ocular Syndrome (SANS) optic nerve swelling early via interactive Amsler grid eye checks and prevents astronaut alarm panic by keeping psychological self-care locally encrypted onboard.

Intended Dual-Horizon Impact On Horizon 1 (Artemis Moon and Mars suits), ASTRO-SHIELD prevents cognitive drift, prefrontal fatigue, and SANS vision loss in isolated crews. On Horizon 2 (Earth), the architecture adapts into a portable nanoconductor headband and dermal patch to deliver zero-internet clinical and mental health triage to rural Texas clinics and disaster zones.

Tools, Programming Languages, Hardware, and Software Hardware architecture integrates non-invasive dry-contact nanoconductor arrays inside the helmet liner and inner suit with zero thermal noise, paired with an in-suit wrist cockpit display running under 5 ms offline latency. Software was built using TypeScript 5, React 18 Progressive Web App (PWA) edge architecture, Web Crypto AES-256 local encryption, and compact under 8 KB FHIR-Lite telemetry packets. Thresholds were calibrated with NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR), NASA Human Research Program (HRP) Standard Measures, Mars One-Way Light Time (14m 22s) standards, and CSA, ESA Concordia, and JAXA space medicine datasets, while AI tools assisted strictly with conceptual studio renders and UI code scaffolding.

How the Project Is Creative Rather than relying on wet clinical electrodes or cloud chatbots that fail in deep space, Team LEXIA embedded dry nanoconductors directly into spacesuit textiles and united three original human-authored frameworks: SAC neuro-harmonization, deterministic VIB triage, and the bioethical Carlota Factor.

Factors Considered by Our Team Our team accounted for Mars signal physics (14m 22s one-way delay), microgravity pathophysiology (over 60% long-flight SANS risk, unbound cortisol and brain adenosine spikes, and 600 mSv career radiation limits), deterministic software safety, and crew bioethics—ensuring astronauts never hide mental distress out of fear of raw ground surveillance.
